source.title: Belfast Telegraph, 3 June 1961, p. 7 ("Notice of Result of Elections: County of Antrim - Election of County Councillors")
source.publisher: Belfast Telegraph (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: 23 divisions, 24 seats (Newtownabbey two): 3 contested (Ballymoney, Carrickfergus, Kirkinriola) and 20 unopposed, all named in the returning officer's notice of result. The notice gives no party labels except where the newspapers print them for the three contests.

note: Triennial election of Antrim County Council on the 23 county electoral divisions, poll Thursday 1 June 1961 (Irish News, 1 May 1961, p. 2, official notice). Nominations were received on 16 May by the returning officer, W. S. Henderson, at the County Courthouse, Crumlin Road, Belfast; withdrawals closed at 3 p.m. on 17 May. Four contests were nominated - Ballymoney, Carrickfergus, Kirkinriola and Portrush - but Mr. G. F. Allingham withdrew from Portrush, where the sitting member, Mr. Charles M'Vicker, was 'returned unopposed' (Belfast News-Letter, 18 May 1961, p. 10), leaving three contests. The returning officer's 'Notice of Result of Elections: County of Antrim - Election of County Councillors for the above-named County in the Year 1961' (Belfast Telegraph, 3 June 1961, p. 7) prints all 23 divisions, the candidates, places of abode, votes recorded and names elected, and is the source for the unopposed returns, whose vote column is blank. No poll; vote column blank. Returned unopposed.
